transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Leah Martinez (Head of ML, NovaDocs), Omar Khalid (SRE, NovaDocs), Marta Ruiz (CTO, NovaDocs)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood serving performance vs their current baseline provider. Discussed latency/throughput numbers, batching and cache tuning, cost delta, dedicated vs hosted choices, and security artifacts. Agreed on next steps: more 95th percentile tests, share pricing and SOC2 docs, collect traffic profile for final pilot sizing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah thanks for the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Leah: Leah here, hi.
[00:07] Omar: Omar here.
[00:09] Marta: Marta, hello.
[00:10] Priya: Priya from Redwood.
[00:12] Jordan: Awesome. So agenda - quick recap of what we ran this week, go through the benchmark sheet, talk tuning changes we tried (batching, quantization profile), and then next steps.

[02:01] Jordan: Priya, do you want to take the bench numbers?
[02:05] Priya: Sure. So we put the latest run into the sheet: https://redwood.in/sheets/poc-novadocs-bench-2026. The key rows are the baseline provider (their on-prem cluster) versus Redwood hosted and a Redwood Dedicated config (small pool). We measured p50/p95 token latencies, tokens-per-second throughput under steady stream qps, and cost-per-1M tokens.

[03:12] Priya: High level - p50 is pretty similar across both for short inference (<=256 tokens). Where we see divergence is p95 for longer sequences and under concurrent streams. Redwood Dedicated on H100-like configs has lower p95 by ~30-40% versus their baseline A100-ish pods for the 1k-2k token tests. For example: baseline p95 for 1k tokens 820ms, Redwood Dedicated p95 540ms. p50s were 120ms vs 110ms.

[04:05] Leah: Hold on - those numbers are lower than I expected. Are those with prefix caching enabled?

[04:11] Priya: Good question. The 1k tests did include prefix/KV cache warmup for repeated prompts; the cold-start runs are also in the sheet under separate tabs. Cold p95 on 1k was 1.2s for baseline and 0.95s for Redwood Dedicated.

[05:00] Omar: What's the request pattern here? We have a lot of micro-conversations, average 300 tokens but occasional long docs of 2k.

[05:06] Jordan: Right, Omar mentioned that last week; we mirrored your traffic profile (see sheet top left). We ran mixed workloads: 70% short (<=300 tokens), 25% mid (300-1k), 5% long (1-2k).

[06:25] Priya: For throughput, under sustained concurrent callers we measured tokens/sec per GPU. Baseline was about 18k tokens/sec per A100 node under our batching config; Redwood Dedicated on H100 config delivered about 26k tokens/sec. That translates to higher headroom for burst and lower per-token cost when we batch effectively.

[07:10] Marta: How reproducible are these? Our ops wants predictable tail latency - p95 is what we care about.

[07:18] Priya: Totally. We've run repeated sweeps and the medians are stable, but tails do vary with sequence mix and caching. That's why we recommended the 95th pct E2E runs - warm KV cache + simulated real traffic - to reflect your real tail behavior.

[08:45] Leah: Can you explain what you changed with batching? We already do some batching on our side, but the provider has a fixed batch window that sometimes increases latency.

[08:52] Priya: Sure. Redwood runtime uses continuous batching with adaptive windowing; we tune max batch size and latency SLO per route. For these tests we used a conservative latency SLO of 150ms for short prompts which keeps p50 low but allows larger batches for throughput. We also tested a "cost-first" profile that increased batch window to improve throughput at the expense of p95.

[10:05] Jordan: Also note we tried quantization profile Q4_0 and Q4_1 on one of the model variants - Q4_1 gave a small perf boost and minimal quality regression for your eval prompts, see eval tab. That reduced memory footprint, letting larger effective batch sizes on a single GPU.

[11:40] Omar: Any issues with tokenization or slight drift in responses when quantized?

[11:45] Priya: We did A/B checks on the prompt set you provided. There were a tiny number of divergence cases (about 0.8% of prompts) which we flagged in evals. We can run a focused quality run for the 2k-long docs if you want.

[13:00] Marta: On security: we need to know data residency options - could Dedicated be VPC-only?

[13:06] Jordan: Yes. Dedicated can be in your VPC or we can do Private deployment. For the Dedicated trial we can set up a private VPC peering and KMS integration. We'll share SOC2 and security checklist after the call.

[14:20] Leah: Cost - what's the per-token delta compared to baseline? Their numbers look cheaper on paper but they don't include autoscaling inefficiencies and preemption.

[14:28] Priya: Exactly. Raw per-token compute cost on baseline when fully utilized was comparable. But baseline's overall cost grows due to lower utilization with small bursts, and their preemptible nodes cause retries. In our sheet we modeled 3-month pilot utilization and included autoscale inefficiencies: Redwood Dedicated came out ~12-18% lower TCO for your workload assumptions. Hosted API is slightly higher but avoids infra ops.

[15:40] Omar: Did you run the 2k token p95 on hosted or dedicated?

[15:44] Priya: Both. Hosted had slightly higher p95 for long sequences compared to Dedicated (about 10-15% worse) because hosted runs a mix of model variants and we prioritize multi-tenant isolation. Dedicated is tuned to your traffic and we can pin model variants and quantization.

[17:00] Leah: One concern - our legal team will push on logs and audit. How long do logs persist with Dedicated?

[17:07] Jordan: Logs and audit retention is configurable; for Dedicated we can keep audit logs for the retention window you need and integrate with your SIEM. We'll include that in the security doc.

[18:25] Priya: I want to call out noise in the measurements - we're seeing occasional background jobs on baseline cluster that spiked p95. We marked those runs as outliers in the sheet; we can re-run if you want completely clean isolations.

[19:10] Marta: Yes please re-run the 95th pct with a clean baseline so we have apples-to-apples.

[19:20] Jordan: Action: Priya will kick off 95th percentile E2E runs that mirror production traffic including cache warmups; Omar will hand over traffic profile and peak concurrency numbers.

[21:35] Omar: One operational question - how does model fallback work if a node is busy? Do you do automated fallback to smaller model variants to preserve latency?

[21:42] Priya: We have smart routing policies. You can configure fallback chains (e.g., rollout to a smaller quantized model or route to a slightly older variant) and set per-route SLOs. That reduces error rates and keeps service up during capacity pressure.

[23:00] Leah: Can we get a quick demo of routing rules? Maybe next week?

[23:04] Jordan: Yep, we can do that. We'll set up a 30-minute SE-led demo to show routing, cache behavior, and the console metrics. Proposed window next Tue.

[24:30] Priya: Back to tuning - we tried raising max_batch_size from 64 to 96 in one trial which improved tokens/sec but increased p95 by 70ms on short prompts. There's a sweet spot around 72 for your mix. Details in the tuning tab.

[26:15] Marta: Regarding quantization, would Q8 be an option for more cost savings?

[26:22] Priya: We don't recommend Q8 for this model family - we saw quality drop on doc summarization prompts. Q4_1 seems best trade-off. We can run a targeted eval if you want further cost-focused runs.

[28:40] Jordan: Quick aside - competitors: you mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier; both have different latency/cost tradeoffs. Anthropic gave competitive quality on instruction tasks but was more expensive at scale in our modeling. OpenAI's hosted endpoints are strong but less flexible for VPC/private deployments.

[30:05] Leah: Ok - recap, what are immediate next steps?

[30:10] Jordan: I'll read them out: 1) Priya to run the E2E p95 tests for 1k-2k sequences with warm cache by 2026-03-30. 2) Jordan to send Dedicated pricing and trial agreement by 2026-03-25. 3) Jordan to share SOC2 and the security checklist by 2026-03-24. 4) Omar to share traffic profile and concurrency metrics by 2026-03-26. 5) Schedule SE demo of routing and console next Tue (Jordan to propose times).

[32:00] Omar: One more - for the p95 runs, please include cold-start with key rotation scenario. We saw issues when keys rotated mid-run.

[32:10] Priya: Noted - we'll include a key rotation scenario in the E2E script.

[33:45] Marta: About pilot sizing - assuming your Dedicated numbers hold, we'd likely start with 4 GPUs and autoscale to 8 for peak. Can you confirm recommended initial pool?

[33:55] Priya: Based on current profile, we recommend starting with 4 H100-class GPUs for the pilot; we'll monitor and autoscale as needed. We'll send a sizing recommendation in the pricing doc.

[35:30] Leah: Anything else on risks?

[35:34] Jordan: Main risks are data residency and audit requirements (we can address with Dedicated/VPC), and tail latency variability - which we'll address with the E2E p95 runs and fallback policies.

[37:00] Jordan: Quick note: some transcription artifacts in our automated notes - "kayvee cache" shows up instead of KV cache in places, and A-one-hundred got transcribed oddly. Please rely on the sheet where numbers are canonical.

[38:10] Marta: Got it.

[40:00] Jordan: Closing - thanks for the feedback. We'll follow up with the docs and runs.
[40:05] Leah: Thanks everyone.
[40:10] Omar: Thanks.
[40:12] Priya: Bye.

Recording end.

References to shared artifacts:
- Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.in/sheets/poc-novadocs-bench-2026 (contains raw runs, tuning tabs, evals)
- Security checklist/SOC2 (to be shared): link placeholder will be added in email

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had medium accuracy; occasional mis-attributions and word swaps (e.g., "kayvee cache" = KV cache). Numbers in the sheet are authoritative.

Recap of key benchmark numbers (copied from sheet for quick ref):
- Short prompts (<=256): p50 Redwood 110ms, baseline 120ms; p95 Redwood 240ms, baseline 260ms
- Mid prompts (300-1k): p50 Redwood 180ms, baseline 200ms; p95 Redwood 420ms, baseline 600ms
- Long prompts (1k-2k): p50 Redwood 520ms, baseline 600ms; p95 Redwood Dedicated 540ms, baseline 820ms (cold: Redwood 950ms, baseline 1200ms)
- Throughput per GPU (mixed workload): Redwood Dedicated ~26k tokens/sec, baseline ~18k tokens/sec
- Modeled TCO delta (pilot conditions): Redwood Dedicated ~12-18% lower over 3 months (includes autoscale inefficiencies)

End of file.
